new_entities.name: Low ferritin
new_entities.description: Reduced ferritin concentration used as a marker of low body iron stores.

edges.effect_quant: Evidence is mixed but directionally leans toward lower ferritin in telogen effluvium cohorts; post-COVID TE case-control data found lower mean ferritin in cases than controls (68.5 vs 137.0 µg/L).
edges.population: women with acute or chronic telogen effluvium
edges.mechanism: Low ferritin reflects reduced iron reserves that can limit matrix-cell proliferation in the hair follicle and make follicles more vulnerable to synchronized shedding under physiologic stress. That pathway is plausible, but telogen effluvium is heterogeneous enough that ferritin is best viewed as one contributor rather than a universal explanation.
edges.summary: Low ferritin is commonly investigated in telogen effluvium and remains a plausible risk signal, but the literature is not uniformly positive. Recent case-control work does not always show a ferritin gap, while other cross-sectional and observational studies support an association and suggest that iron-directed treatment may help at least a subset of patients.
edges.caveats: Ferritin is influenced by inflammation and does not cleanly separate cause from consequence in every shedding disorder. This edge is therefore intentionally conservative and should be read as a likely contributor in some TE patients, not a defining biomarker for all cases.

evidence.citation: Durusu Turkoglu IN et al 2024 J Cosmet Dermatol
evidence.notes: A comprehensive investigation of biochemical status in patients with telogen effluvium: Analysis of Hb, ferritin, vitamin B12, vitamin D, thyroid function tests, zinc, copper, biotin, and selenium levels.

evidence.citation: Cheung EJ et al 2016 J Drugs Dermatol
